title: This week in India's growth story: October 26-November 1, 2026
excerpt: A week of 31 stories: a 164 GW solar milestone, a Rs 12,000 crore comeback from a wiped-out factory, a record wind power year, a train with no engine, a trillion-dollar export target turning into arithmetic, and a record month for electric scooters - alongside the people who kept building through all of it.
bodyHtml:
Thirty-one stories this week, and the pattern that kept surfacing was recovery and reinvention - a factory wiped out and rebuilt bigger, a farmer's quiet five-year transformation finally noticed, a district getting its first train after 80 years, a career redirected into something nobody expected. Here's the week, day by day.

Monday, October 26

India crossed 164 gigawatts of solar capacity, a nearly 57-fold increase since 2014. On this day in 1890, a journalist was born who gave Bhagat Singh his first writing job - and died trying to stop a riot. Dr. Soumya Swaminathan became only the second Indian woman ever elected a Fellow of the Royal Society. Canadian radio stations raised $2 million CAD for Punjab flood relief in two days. And a banker walked away from two decades of security at 49 to start Nykaa - now India's wealthiest self-made woman.

Tuesday, October 27

Delhi Airport had its busiest half-year ever, with 38.5 million passengers. On this day in 1904, Jatindra Nath Das was born - a freedom fighter who later died demanding dignity for prisoners during a 63-day hunger strike. Mahesh Kakde was recognized with the 2026 Ramanujan Prize. Asha Jadeja Motwani funded a $5 million American Studies institute at JGU. And an entrepreneur who lost everything rebuilt from Sri Lanka outward into a Rs 12,000 crore company.

Wednesday, October 28

India had its best-ever year for wind power capacity in FY26. On this day in 1627, Mughal emperor Jahangir died - his wife Nur Jahan having run half his empire. Anuparna Roy won her second Venice NETPAC award in two years. A one-night gala for VOSAP raised $214,000 for disabled Indians. And a Mizoram farmer who started growing strawberries in 2024 was named a UN global hero after just two years in the field.

Thursday, October 29

India's coffee exports crossed a record $2.1 billion before the fiscal year even closed. On this day in 2018, Train 18 - the prototype for what became the Vande Bharat Express - was unveiled, built with no separate engine. Pulkit Desai became the first Indian-American mayor of Parsippany-Troy Hills, New Jersey. And a cotton farmer's quiet five-year transformation toward regenerative soil practices finally got industry recognition.

Friday, October 30

A rail line to Sidhi district brought the region its first train connectivity since Independence - an 80-year wait. On this day in 1909, Homi Bhabha was born, a physicist whose career built both India's premier research institute and its nuclear program. Tammy Sandhu, a diplomat's daughter, became the UK's Ambassador to the Holy See. And a boy who gave private tuitions to support his family built PhysicsWallah into an edtech company - landing him on Forbes' billionaires list in 2026.

Saturday, October 31

Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India's $1 trillion FY27 export target was turning from aspiration into arithmetic, with April-August exports already up over 15% year-on-year. On this day in 1875, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born - the man who negotiated over 500 princely states into one country, marked every year since 2014 as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Kanishka Narayan, born in Bihar, became the UK's first dedicated AI Minister. And a Gujarat farm worker who trained as a solar technician was praised by name on Mann Ki Baat.

Sunday, November 1

India registered a record 223,886 electric two-wheelers in a single month, up 48% year-on-year. On this day, Karnataka Rajyotsava marks a state born on November 1, 1956 and renamed on the very same date 17 years later, in 1973. Ashutosh Chilkoti, India-trained at IIT Delhi, was elected to the US National Academy of Medicine. And a Manipur craftswoman's bamboo and wood workshop, now employing more than 50 artists, got a mention from the Prime Minister himself.

Thirty-one stories, one week. A solar milestone, a record wind year, a coffee export record and a record month for electric scooters - alongside the quiet five-year transformations, the 80-year waits, and the career pivots that finally got their moment.

coverHeadlines: India just crossed 164 gigawatts of solar power. That's the world's third-largest installed solar capacity.
Delhi's airport just had its busiest first half of a fiscal year ever. 38.5 million passengers in six months.
India just had its best year ever for wind power. A record that stood for nearly a decade just fell.
India's coffee exports just had their best year ever. Over $2.1 billion in a single fiscal year.
A Madhya Pradesh district just got its first railway line since Independence. Nearly 80 years without one.
India's commerce minister says a $1 trillion export target is within reach. And the first half of the year backs him up.
India just registered a record number of electric two-wheelers in a single month. 223,886 of them, in October alone.
